software.name: temporal-gamma-index
software.title: The γ-index: tolerance-based validation of spatio-temporal forecast fields (MATLAB)

article.citation: C. Voyant. A tolerance-based framework for spatiotemporal forecast validation using the γ-index. International Journal of Forecasting 42(4) (2026) 1207–1214

supported: validate a gridded forecast against observed fields with physical tolerances
compare forecast fields with GPR and mean γ
out_of_scope: point time series without a spatial grid

inputs.definition: spatial tolerance; the article uses one grid spacing (≈ 2 km)
temporal tolerance; the article uses 30 min (Δt/2 with interpolation)
intensity tolerance; the article uses 50 W/m² (about 10 %)
pixel size before and after rescaling (km per pixel)
time between images before and after interpolation (hours)

rules: Never invent a value. Each input is given by the user, an exact unit conversion of a given value, or a documented default that the user explicitly accepts.
Use the canonical unit of each field; convert exactly and say so (for example 2 km -> 2000 m). Never mix a percentage and a fraction.
Ask when a request is ambiguous or a required input is missing; do not infer a number from a place name or a qualitative word.
Run the code unmodified. Report only what was actually computed, with quantity, unit and the input values used; never present a planned or unavailable run as a result.
State the scope and the limits below when you report a result.
The article proposes GPR > 80 % and mean γ < 0.7 as practical thresholds; keep the bias (MBE) and pointwise errors alongside.
In the article a ±50 % change of DTA, TTA or IDT changed GPR by less than 10 % and mean γ by less than 0.3 (Corsica conditions).
limits: Implementation note: computeGammaMetrics.m measures distances in grid cells and image steps, then divides them by DTA (km) and TTA (minutes). Give maps on a 1 km grid (res_ini = res_end = 1) and set timestep_end = 1/60 h, or convert the tolerances to cells and steps.
The temporal component was not fully exploited in the article (validation mostly spatial); DTA = 1 pixel suits 1 to 5 km grids.
The tolerances are application choices to report with the results.
execution_notice: This descriptor documents the software. It is not a registered WebSemantic adapter, an executable API, or evidence that the full scientific workflow has been validated.
